history.change: added 24 July 2026 via the coverage audit: Storm Claudia winter 2025-26 flooding, ~400 homes, 2 million emergency funding; verified against the Welsh Government flood Written Statement 27 Feb 2026
corrected Storm Claudia date from December to November 2025 at adversarial verification; the Welsh Government Written Statement itself carries the wrong month, Met Office/NRW confirm 14-15 November
Imported from the NRW SI horizon register (signals.json, scan date 2026-07-25). Grading defaulted on import and awaits analyst review.

notes: The flood side of the drought, fire and flood whiplash the report describes: the register carried the flood-risk funding programme (fcerm-programme-2026-27) but not the acute events. Threatens SI8. Found via the July 2026 coverage audit; a flood-event query was added to the people and place cluster. Note: the Welsh Government Written Statement misdates Storm Claudia as December 2025; the Met Office, JBA and NRW's own 15 November 2025 statement confirm it struck Wales on 14 to 15 November 2025. The register uses the correct date.
summary: Storm Claudia flooded almost 400 homes and businesses across Caerphilly, Denbighshire, Powys, Torfaen, Rhondda Cynon Taf and Newport in November 2025, with further winter flooding in Monmouth, Skenfrith and Carmarthenshire. Almost 2 million pounds in emergency capital flood funding was issued. A Welsh Government Written Statement (27 February 2026) records more than 377 million pounds committed to flood risk management this Senedd term, with over 85 million for 2026-27.
title: Winter 2025-26 flooding hits about 400 Welsh homes (Storm Claudia), the flood side of the climate whiplash
